prerequisites: Basic knowledge of production processes, industrial manufacturing and assembly procedures and their planning.

learning_outcomes.text: Students differentiate between common production-related simulation tools and describe their use in the production environment. They explain the functionality of various simulation programs and identify expected accuracies and inaccuracies in conducting simulation studies.

Students apply selected simulation tools purposefully and independently conduct simulation studies on production-relevant tasks. They critically reflect on the results derivable from simulation studies and organize their implementation in the production environment in the sense of continuous improvement management.

Students select relevant data (including mass data) for simulation studies and analyze them with a view to implementing suitable simulation models. They prove the correctness of the created simulation models through verification and validation based on scientific findings from specialist literature and case studies. In this context, students also design research questions for the further development of simulation tools and the appropriate application methodology.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals: production-related simulation techniques and tools, conducting simulation studies, simulation tools in the Digital Factory
Forming simulation: strategies, non-linear Finite Element Method, material properties, contact conditions, process flow
Welding simulation: Radaj triangle, heat conduction models, distortion, residual stresses, simulation process
Plastic injection molding simulation: fundamentals, analysis possibilities, meshing methods, process of a simulation investigation
Painting simulation: particle flow vs. coating process, process and workpiece modeling, result representation
Robot simulation: overview of simulation tools, Realistic Robot Simulation, collision-avoiding path planning, offline path/program creation
Human simulation and ergonomics analyses: human model, biomechanics, movement definition, analysis methods
Event-oriented simulation: areas of application, mode of operation, data preparation, result evaluation
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance will be determined by the lecturers: written examination or oral examination. The ungraded examination performance consists of 3 to 5 experimental tasks within the framework of the experimental work. For the written examination, the applicable study regulations apply. For the oral examination, the applicable General Part of the examination regulations applies.
